Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

property noun

a house or land

also real estate, a property, estate, land, property prices, buy a property, real estate broker, estate agent, realtor

classical

Cato Agr. 1.1: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis
Cic. Rosc. Com. 33: cum jacērent pretia praediōrum, when property prices were low
Traupman 369

praedium, praediī n.

noun, second declension

a property, an estate, in town or country

Land or buildings owned: praedium urbānum, a building in town (Cic. Verr. 2.3.199, Lewis & Short); praedium rūsticum, land in the country (Nep. Att. 14.3).

Other words

  • possessiō, possessiōnis f. — a property, an estate (often plural)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Nep. Att. 14.3: in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus; Cic. Rosc. Com. 33: omnium possessiōnēs erant incertae

  • fundus, fundī m. — a farm, a piece of land

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 2.1; Traupman 166

  • praediātor, praediātōris m. — dealer in landed property; Traupman: real-estate broker

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.14 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 369

    Classically one who bought estates sold at auction for debt (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • praedium quom parāre cōgitābis, sīc in animō habētō: utī nē cupidē emās nēve operā tuā parcās vīsere et nē satis habeās semel circumīre

    when you are thinking of buying a property, keep this in mind: don’t buy in a hurry, don’t spare yourself the trouble of going to see it, and don’t think it enough to walk round it onceCato Agr. 1.1

  • Accēpit enim agrum temporibus eīs cum jacērent pretia praediōrum

    for he took over the land at a time when property prices were lowCic. Rosc. Com. 33

  • rēs solī

    real estateTraupman 369

See also house, property, income, buy.
